findings.topic: Primitive class of an essential disc
findings.assessment: Valid under the stated orientable one-vertex, first-Betti-number-one, unique-torus-boundary setting. A boundary curve crossing the essential disc boundary once pushes into a collar to pair to one with the dual class. Rank-one integral H1 duality makes this primitive class plus or minus the chosen primitive cocycle class. One vertex makes every integral vertex coboundary zero.

For an already validated nonzero admissible standard-coordinate vector, nullity one of the matching matrix on positive support is exactly the vertex-ray criterion used here. A nonzero maximal minor together with the supplied kernel vector certifies this nullity without approximate rank.

The face-corner and opposite-edge four-point formulas are consistent in all three quadrilateral sectors. Identifying local edge occurrences cannot increase the coefficient l1 bound used for the finite hyperplane family.

Every leaf has probability at least exp(-R) under uniform child choices, giving at most exp(R) leaves. Height H bounds the union of root-to-leaf paths by (H+1) times that number. The article explicitly charges failed attempts, restarts, and unary runs.

The discovery inequality r log(n+1)+k log(d+1)=O(log(n+1)^2), together with the stated polynomial source/bit-size assumptions, implies n^{O(log n)}. The two substitutions into 2^{O(s^3)} poly(L) are algebraically correct and explicitly conditional.

Current wording correctly concerns attached bordered bases and existence of exactly one additional relative two-handle per saturated base. It does not count pre-existing core two-handles or claim an implemented attaching-curve transport. The source-chart/core/resource-limit caveat is explicitly restricted to the unmarked census.
